newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Rhone-Poulenc/Hoechst set recall.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Rhone-Poulenc/Hoechst set recall.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc said Thursday that its Centeon LLC joint venture with Germany's Hoechst AG is voluntarily recalling all its in-date lots of albumin products as a precaution against risk of bacterial infection.
This is the full text of the announcement.

COLLEGEVILLE, Pa., Oct. 10 /PRNewswire/ -- Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc. (NYSE: RPR) stated today that Centeon L.L.C., a joint venture company of RPR and Hoechst A.G., has announced a voluntary worldwide recall of all in-date lots of its albumin products (Albuminar(R) and Plasma Plex(R)). Centeon is taking this action as a precaution against risk of bacterial contamination related to vials cracked in transit. No other Centeon products are affected by this voluntary action.

RPR estimates that, based on preliminary information, the negative impact of the recall combined with the potential impact of lost sales, could reduce the consensus earnings estimate for full year 1996 by around 10-12 percent.
Albumin is a volume expander that is often used in critical care settings such as surgery and in the treatment of shock, trauma and burns.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer is a global pharmaceutical company dedicated to improving human health.
